messages:
From: Rajiv Menon <rajiv@heliosanalytics.com>
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 14 Sep 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Burst behavior during nightly ETL runs - Dedicated cluster sizing

Hi Hannah,

Quick question as we finish the procurement checklist: our nightly ETL overlay (data enrichment + reranking) causes token/sec spikes for about 20-30 minutes between 01:00-01:45 UTC. Current observed peak is ~4k tokens/sec (mostly short responses, high QPS).

We're interested in Redwood Dedicated but worried about how burst capacity will behave during those windows. Specifically:
- If we provision a 8-GPU reserved slab, can we reliably burst to an additional 12 GPUs for those 30-minute windows?
- How would autoscaling interact with billing and preemptible resources? We need predictable upper bounds for SRE and budget.
- Any recommended fallbacks if GPU headroom is exhausted (quantized fallback model, shorter context, queueing)?

Also cc'ing procurement for contract-level constraints. Happy to jump on a 30-min call if that's easier.

Thanks,
Rajiv
Rajiv Menon
Head of Platform
Helios Analytics

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Rajiv Menon <rajiv@heliosanalytics.com>
Date: Fri, 14 Sep 2028 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Burst behavior during nightly ETL runs - Dedicated cluster sizing

Hi Rajiv — thanks, this is exactly the kind of detail that helps us size properly. Summary below of a proposed approach; attaching a short capacity proposal (helios_capacity_proposal_v1.pdf) with numbers and monthly cost ranges.

Proposal (high level)
- Baseline reserved: 8 GPUs (sized for your daytime P95 latency and sustained throughput).
- Tiered burst headroom: allow automatic ephemerally-attached GPUs up to 12 additional GPUs (total cap = 20 GPUs) for short windows.
- Preemptible fallback: when ephemerals are unavailable, route new requests to a quantized v2 model (int8) that uses ~40% less GPU memory and runs ~1.6x faster for short contexts.
- Rate-based queueing: if cluster reaches hard cap, accepted requests beyond soft limit enter a short priority queue (max queue time 45s) with graceful 429/429-with-retry headers for client handling.

Autoscale policy (recommended defaults)
- scale_min: 8 GPUs; scale_max: 20 GPUs
- scale_step: 2 GPUs per 30s (prevents thrash)
- cool_down: 90s after scale-out, 600s after scale-in (favor keeping warmed KV cache)
- headroom_budget: 1800 GPU-minutes per day (configurable monthly) to control costs
- preemptible_pool_pct: 60% of burst pool (so at most ~7 of 12 burst GPUs may be preemptible)

Operational notes
- KV cache warming: we recommend a small warm-up run (5—10 minutes) prior to your ETL window to reduce early-LLM latency.
- Observability: enable per-route token accounting and per-GPU utilization dashboards so we can refine headroom_budget over the first 2 billing cycles.

If that aligns, I'll run this past the engineering team for any constraints and send a final MOU-ready sizing table.

Next steps
- Your team: confirm preferred hard cap and maximum budget tolerance for burst minutes.
- Ours: I will share a refined cost model and an MOU draft.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Sales Lead, Dedicated
Redwood Inference

Attachment: helios_capacity_proposal_v1.pdf (proposal, diagrams, monthly run-rate ranges)

Quick notes from infra/SE perspective:
- Agree with conservative step sizing, but suggest scale_step=4 GPUs / 60s for more predictable burst ramp (reduces overshoot when many short bursts occur).
- Recommend raising pre-warm to 10 minutes and running a small synthetic load 12 minutes before the ETL window to populate KV caches (we can script this).
- headroom_budget: convert to monthly cap as well (example: 54,000 GPU-min/month) so procurement can map to billing forecasts.
- Preemptible behavior: set a policy to avoid routing latency-critical routes to preemptible instances. Mark routes as "non-evictable" in the canary period.
- Eviction handling: on preemptible reclaim, automatically lower context window to 1024 tokens for affected requests and annotate responses with header X-Redwood-Fallback: quantized-v2.

Attached a quick cost model that maps burst minutes to projected monthly spend (gpu-cost-model-helio.xlsx).

If those look good I'll align with SRE on runbook language and suggested SLA exceptions for scheduled ETL windows.

cheers,
Ben Carter
Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

Rajiv — thanks again for the details and patience while we looped in engineering. We have an agreed configuration and next steps below. I also attached the MOU and cost workbook for signatures and internal routing.

Agreed configuration (final)
- Reserved slab: 8 GPUs (as discussed)
- Burst pool: up to 12 additional GPUs (scale_max = 20)
- Autoscale behavior: scale_step = 4 GPUs / 60s (to reduce overshoot), cool_down out = 120s, cool_down in = 600s
- Headroom caps: 54,000 GPU-min/month (configurable), default per-day soft budget of 1,800 GPU-min/day
- Preemptible policy: up to 60% of burst pool; mark latency-critical routes as non-evictable during pilot windows
- Fallbacks: quantized-v2 fallback (context limit 1024 tokens) + short queue (max 45s) before returning 429

Operational next steps
1) Procurement: please review and confirm acceptable headroom cap mapping to your budget (we included a range in the workbook).
2) Technical: we'll run a KV warm-up script 12 minutes prior to your ETL window during the pilot week.
